neighbours.label: hedged possibility: a modal or adverb that marks a claim as uncertain (may well, probably, could, perhaps)
fire: Historians think the manuscript may well date from the ninth century.
The ancient wall was probably built to keep out raiders.
Such a large crater could only have come from a meteor.
The painter's model was perhaps his younger sister.
In all likelihood the river once flowed further east.
The tools might have belonged to a travelling smith.
This tribe possibly reached the coast before the Romans.
The odd marks may have been left by grazing deer.
quiet: Historians know the manuscript dates from the ninth century.
The ancient wall was built in 1205 to keep out raiders.
This large crater came from a meteor in 1908.
The painter's model was his younger sister Anna.
Records show the river once flowed further east.
The tools belonged to a travelling smith named Hugh.
This tribe reached the coast before the Romans.
The odd marks were left by grazing deer last spring.

notes: card: peaks on ' may', ' probably', ' could', ' Perhaps', 'In all probability'; logit effect promotes likely/probably/perhaps. Probes 0.08-0.21, so the median may fall short.
